Also spelled ''ancle''.

'''ankle-bone''' (ang′kl-bōn), ''n.'' The bone of the ankle; the astragalus or huckle-bone.

'''ankle-boot''' (ang′kl-böt), ''n.'' '''1.''' A covering for the ankle of a horse, designed to prevent interfering. See ''interfere''.—'''2.''' A boot reaching a little above a person’s ankle.

'''ankle-clonus''' (ang′kl-klō″nus), ''n.'' The clonic spasm of the calf-muscles evoked in certain cases by a sudden bending of the foot upward toward the ankle, to such an extent as to render the tendon of Achilles very tense.

'''ankled''' (ang′kld), ''a.'' [< ''ankle'' + ''-ed''<sup>2</sup>.] Having ankles: used in composition: as, well-''ankled''.

'''ankle-deep''' (ang′kl-dēp), ''a.'' '''1.''' Sunk in water, mud, or the like, up to the ankles.—'''2.''' Of a depth sufficient to reach or come up to the top of the ankle.

'''ankle-jack''' (ang′kl-jak), ''n.'' A kind of boot reaching above the ankle.
{{smaller block|He [Captain Cuttle] put on an unparalleled pair of ''ankle-jacks.''
{{right|''Dickens'', Dombey and Son, xv.}}}}

'''ankle-jerk''' (ang′kl-jėrk), ''n.'' The contraction of the muscles of the calf caused by striking the tendon of Achilles just above the heel or sud-
readings.c1s2:
denly stretching it. Also called ''ankle-reflex.''

'''ankle-joint''' (ang′kl-joint), ''n.'' '''1.''' In ordinary language, same as ''ankle'', 1.—'''2.''' In ''zoöl.'' and ''anat.'', the tarsal joint. (''a'') In mammals, the tibiotarsal articulation. (''b'') In other vertebrates, the mediotarsal articulation. See ''tarsal, tarsus.''

'''ankle-reflex''' (ang′kl-rē″fleks), ''n.'' Same as ''ankle-jerk.''

'''anklet''' (ang′klet), ''n.'' [< ''ankle'' + dim. ''-et.''] '''1.''' A little ankle.—'''2.''' An ornament for the ankle, corresponding to the bracelet for the wrist or forearm.—'''3.''' A support or brace for the leg, intended to stiffen the ankle-joint and prevent the ankle from turning to one side.—'''4.''' An extension of the top of a boot or shoe, designed sometimes for protection to a weak ankle, sometimes merely for ornament.—'''5.''' A fetter or shackle for the ankles.
{{smaller block|To every bench, as a fixture, there was a chain with heavy ''anklets.''
{{right|''L. Wallace'', Ben-Hur, p. 152.}}}}

'''ankle-tie''' (ang′kl-tī), ''n.'' A kind of slipper with straps buttoning around the ankle.

In ''anat.'' and ''zoöl.'', the consolidation or fusion of two or more bones in one, or the union of the different parts of a bone; bony union; synosteosis: as, the ''ankylosis'' of the cranial bones one with another; the ''ankylosis'' of the different elements of the temporal bone; the ''ankylosis'' of an epiphysis with the shaft of a bone.—'''2.''' In ''pathol.'', stiffness and immovability of a joint; morbid adhesion of the articular ends of contiguous bones.
{{smaller block|He moves along stiffly . . . as the man who, as we are told in the Philosophical Transactions, was afflicted with an universal ''anchylosis''.
{{right|''Goldsmith'', Criticisms.}}}}

'''ann†''', ''n.'' [For ''annat'', ''annet'', appar. with direct ref. to L. ''annus'', a year: see ''annat'', ''annate''.] Same as ''annat''.

'''anna<sup>1</sup>''' (an′ä), ''n.'' [Anglo-Ind., also spelled ''ana'', < Hind. ''ānā''.] In India, the sixteenth part of a rupee, or about 3 cents. {{smaller|Under Queen Victoria, coins of the value of 2 annas (silver), worth 2⅜''d.'', half an anna (copper), etc., have been issued.}}

'''anna<sup>2</sup>''' (an′ä), ''n.'' [S. Amer.] The Indian name of a South American skunk. ''De la Vega.''

'''annabergite''' (an′ạ-bėrg-īt), ''n.'' [< ''Annaberg'', a town in Saxony, + ''-ite''<sup>2</sup>.] A hydrous arseniate of nickel, a massive or earthy mineral of an apple-green color, often resulting from the alteration of arsenides of nickel.

'''annal''' (an′ạl), ''n.'' [In sense 1, a sing. made from pl. ''annals'', q. v. In sense 2, < ML. ''annalis'' (sc. ''missa''), also neut. ''annale'', a mass, < L. ''annalis'', yearly. Cf. {{smaller block|A last-year’s ''annal.''
{{right|''Warburton'', Causes of Prodigies, p. 59.}}}}
'''2.''' Same as ''annual'', ''n.'', 1.

'''annalist''' (an′ạl-ist), ''n.'' [< ''annal'' + ''-ist''; = F. ''annaliste''.] A writer of annals.

'''annatto''' (a-nat′ō), ''n.'' Same as ''arnotto''.

'''anneal<sup>1</sup>''' (a-nēl′), ''v. t.'' [Now spelled in imitation of L. words in ''ann-''; prop., as in early mod. E., ''aneal'', < ME. ''anelen'', ''onelen'', inflame, heat, melt, burn, < AS. ''anǣlan'', ''onǣlan'', burn, < ''an'', ''on'', on, + ''ǣlan'', burn, set on fire, < ''āl'', also ''ǣl'', fire, a burning (a rare word; cf. ''alfet''); cf. ''ǣled'', fire, = OS. ''eld'' = Icel. ''eldr'' = Sw. ''eld'' = Dan. ''ild'', fire (the vowel short, though orig. long). The particular sense ‘enamel’ may have been derived in part from OF. ''neeler'', ''nieler'', later ''neller'', varnish, enamel, orig. paint in black upon gold or silver, < ML. ''nigellare'', blacken, enamel in black, < ''nigellum'', a black enamel (> E. ''niello'', q. v.), < LL. ''nigellus'', blackish, dim. of L. ''niger'', black: see ''negro''.] '''1†.''' Originally, to set on fire; kindle.—'''2†.''' To heat, fire, bake, or fuse, as glass, earthenware, ores, etc.—'''3.''' To heat, as glass, earthenware, or metals, in order to fix colors; enamel.—'''4.''' To treat, as glass, earthenware, or metals, by heating and gradually cooling, so as to toughen them and remove their brittleness.

'''anneal<sup>2</sup>†''', ''v. t.'' Same as ''aneal''<sup>2</sup>.

'''annealer''' (ạ-nē′lėr), ''n.'' One who or that which anneals.

'''annealing''' (ạ-nē′ling), ''n.'' [Early mod. E. also ''anealing''; verbal n. of ''anneal''<sup>1</sup>.] '''1.''' The process or art of treating substances by means of heat, so as to remove their brittleness and at the same time render them tough and more or less elastic. {{smaller|In general, these results are obtained by heating to a high temperature and then cooling very gradu-}}
